# Motion Studies

> A catalogue of authored works and research about transport, geography, and the patterns that movement reveals.

Each work begins with a place, a data source, and a visual claim. Scheduled movement uses timetables and interpolated journeys; observed movement uses broadcast positions and smoothed trajectories; reconstructed movement uses aggregate flow and speed rather than individual tracking.

## Catalogue

- [Motion Studies](https://motionstudies.app/): Catalogue, descriptions of the works, and the approach to scheduled, observed, and reconstructed movement.

## Live studies

- [Gleislicht](https://motionstudies.app/gleislicht/): Switzerland's national clockwork revealed through rail, terrain, Takt, air, and road.
- [All Change](https://motionstudies.app/allchange/): Physical London transforms into Beck-space while journeys continue uninterrupted.
- [Correspondances](https://motionstudies.app/correspondances/): Paris Métro circulation and outward RER movements explore the relationship between centre and banlieue.

## Research studies

- [LUFT](https://luft.motionstudies.app/): A recorded day of European aircraft movement, routes, airport rhythms, and accumulating traces.
- [PFAD](https://pfad.motionstudies.app/): A road search replayed at human scale, revealing the chosen route and the paths not taken.

## Optional

- [Widget lab](https://motionstudies.app/lab/): Interactive lab for shared Motion Studies widgets.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/emmettl/motionstudies): Source code, shared packages, and project documentation.
